newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer, helped by dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer, helped by dlr gains.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened firmer on Thursday, helped by a stronger Canadian dollar and gains in Canadian and U.S. bond markets, analysts said.

"U.S. treasuries are a little bit stronger here. The Canadian dollar is seeing some improvement as well, so that's sort of helped things," said one dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "I don't think the market is going to run away here, but we're seeing a little bit of buying coming in."
Canada's three-month cash T-bill firmed to yield 3.04 percent from 3.05 percent at Wednesday's close.

Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3785 (US$0.7254) in light trading on Thursday after the unit rallied last night in overseas trading. Traders said the dollar benefited from a market belief that the governing Liberals had consolidated their electoral strength days before the June 2 national ballot.
T-bill dealers said the market was relatively active, due partly to settlement transactions linked to Tuesday's weekly T-bill auction.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.39 percent from 3.44 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.92 percent from 3.95 percent.
The call loan rate traded at 3.15 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
